decision_conditions: <p>The proposal to demolish an existing dwelling and replace with a new dwelling,&nbsp; due to its design and excessive scale would harm the special character and appearance of this part of the Pinner Hill Conservation Area. There is not clear and convincing justification for the demolition of the existing dwelling in the Conservation Area, nor identifiable public benefits to outweigh the harm the proposed development poses contrary to the requirements of Section 72 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, Paragraphs 202, 207, 210, 212, 213, 215, 216 and 219 of the NPPF (2024),&nbsp; Policy HC1C of the London Plan (2021), Policy CS1 of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policy DM 7 of the Development Management Plan and Pinner Hill Conservation Area Appraisal and Management Strategy.&nbsp;</p>

<p>There is a general presumption against inappropriate development and development which adversely affects the openness of the Green Belt. The proposed development to demolish and redevelop the site does not comply with relevant guidelines and there is no proven evidence of the existence of ‘very special circumstances'.&nbsp; Therefore the proposed development would conflict with national, strategic and local planning policies regarding Green Belt as set out in the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G2 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CS.1 of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012) and Policy DM 16 of the Development Management Plan Local Policies (2013).&nbsp;</p>
description: Replacement two storey dwelling (Demolition of attached garage, rear of house and front entrance canopy)
